coverage_note: Template recap, 'IODB is the star-bar problem' and the count (n+m)!/(n!m!) were readable; empty-boxes-allowed/not and the Stirling/Bell material were past the cut.
concepts: IODB is the stars-and-bars problem: n identical stars, m identical bars, counted as (n+m)!/(n!m!).
Both groups are internally identical, so both factorials go in the denominator.
The instructor calls this the highest-yield combinatorics template for GATE (his words, not a verified claim about the exam).

gate_claims.claim: A large number of GATE questions come from the IODB / stars-and-bars template.
